findings.title: Denial-cache hit prevents newly granted permissions from being observed
findings.body: A denial entry is returned before consulting either the permission cache or the database, and there is no invalidation when a role, team membership, or resource permission is granted. Consequently, if a Check is denied just before or during creation of a dashboard/folder or an IAM permission update, subsequent checks for that exact resource remain denied for `shortCacheTTL` (30 seconds), even though the DB would now authorize them. This defeats the new stale-cache fallback for the case it is intended to solve. Either invalidate denial keys on permission/resource changes or do not use a denial entry to bypass the DB recheck for newly mutable permissions.

findings.title: Denial-cache key is ambiguous for UIDs containing underscores
findings.body: The key concatenates `name` and `parent` with an unescaped underscore, so distinct resource/folder pairs can produce the same cache key (for example name `a_b` with parent `c`, and name `a` with parent `b_c`). Since dashboard and folder UIDs can contain underscores, a denial for one pair can incorrectly deny another pair for 30 seconds. Encode the fields unambiguously (for example length-prefixing or structured encoding) before using them in the cache key.
